description:
EmailComparator (jmap-mail-types/src/query.rs:310) declares:

    #[serde(default = "bool_true", skip_serializing_if = "is_true")]
    pub is_ascending: bool,

Result: is_ascending is omitted from wire when ascending (the default), present only when descending. Matches the JMAP spec convention that defaults are omittable.

TaskComparator, TaskNotificationComparator, CalendarEventComparator, and ContactCardComparator all declare:

    #[serde(default = "default_ascending")]
    pub is_ascending: bool,

Result: always emitted, even when ascending.

Wire-format spec-conformant in both cases (RFC 8620 §5.5 default is true; receivers must treat absent as ascending). But this is a cross-crate wire-format divergence that downstream HTTP-diff tools, snapshot tests, and content-hash schemes will notice.

EmailComparator is the workspace canonical for the extension-types family (workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates'). The propagation direction is therefore: apply skip_serializing_if = "is_true" + default = "bool_true" to the 3 extension-types sibling comparators (TaskComparator, TaskNotificationComparator, CalendarEventComparator, ContactCardComparator).

Trigger: JMAP-glx8.6 contacts-types review noted the per-crate inconsistency. JMAP-glx8.4 closed the contacts-vs-siblings derive divergence by aligning contacts to the (Tasks, Calendars) camp; this bead is the opposite-direction propagation to align all four extension-types siblings to EmailComparator.
title: Workspace API: comparator is_ascending wire-format skip behavior diverges between mail-types (skip) and 3 extension-types siblings (always-emit)
